text:
maria (Finance): Heads up — seeing ~48 invoices created overnight in NetSuite with missing tax code and blank class. All came from the same webhook window. Not sure if retrying events double-applied any promo credits. Anyone on billing ops awake?

jamie (Billing Ops): Ugh, I noticed ~10 of those had a $0.00 tax line showing in Stripe, but NetSuite import left the tax field empty. The invoice numbers look sequential.

kevin (Eng): I pulled webhook deliveries from the proxy and Stripe. There are 3 deliveries for the same event id with different idempotency headers. Proxy retried while our webhook forwarder also retried. See snippet:```
stripe_event_id=evt_1Kkxx123
delivery=1 status=200 idempotency=abc123
delivery=2 status=200 idempotency=abc123
delivery=3 status=200 idempotency=abc123-retry
```
Looks like the final delivery got a mutated idempotency token so the invoice import job treated it as a new event.

stripe-bot: webhook evt_1Kkxx123 delivered to /webhooks/stripe 3 times (2 successful deliveries, 1 retry). More details at https://dashboard.stripe.com/webhooks

olivia (Revenue Ops): We also had a pricing experiment running that applies a one-time credit for certain plans. If the import job re-applied the same charge event as new, the credit hook might have fired twice for some customers. We flagged 6 customers with duplicate credits in the ledger.

maria (Finance): Yikes. Can we list affected invoice ids so we can mark for manual review before NetSuite send? I don't want those credits exported.

jamie (Billing Ops): Pulling IDs now from nightly importer: INV-2026-3125 .. INV-2026-3162 (48 invoices). The ones with duplicate credits: INV-2026-3131, 3134, 3147, 3152, 3159, 3161.

kevin (Eng): Action plan: 1) Stop the nightly NetSuite push for the affected window (we can pause the job). 2) Rollback the importer to the previous idempotency check that keys off Stripe event id only (temp). 3) Add detection to reject deliveries where idempotency token changes mid-retry. I'll open a PR and an incident.

maria (Finance): Please do not push any of those invoices until we reconcile credits. I can run a diff export from Stripe and mark which credits need reversal.

finance-bot: nightly-reconciliation flagged duplicates in ledger for 6 customers. Job run id: recon-2034567800. See /recon/reports/recon-2034567800.csv

kevin (Eng): Created ticket INF-5019: "mutated-idempotency -> duplicate-imports -> duplicate-credits" and a short rollback PR (link: https://git.internal/redwood/billing/pulls/432). Pausing NetSuite push now. @oncall-eng can you review the cluster proxy logs for any related proxy-side retries?

jamie (Billing Ops): Thanks. I'll start compiling manual adjustment requests for the 6 customers and send to ops for approval. Also we should ask Stripe support if their webhook resend flow can change idempotency headers.

olivia (Revenue Ops): FYI finance team, I'll schedule a quick sync at 11:30 to decide reversals vs invoice credit memos.

maria (Finance): One more note — some of the affected invoices had taxes on the Stripe side, but because NetSuite import was triggered twice the second import omitted tax mapping. We should reconcile tax gross vs net before any exports.

kevin (Eng): Agreed. I'll follow up on the PR and add a small integration test to simulate triple deliveries with mutated headers. We'll also add a monitor to alert if the importer receives the same stripe_event_id with different idempotency tokens in a 10m window.

jamie (Billing Ops): Logged manual ticket BILL-987 for the NetSuite cleanup and attached list of invoice ids.

maria (Finance): Perfect. Thanks everyone. Please add any customer emails to the ticket so support can prep comms if needed. :pray:
